headline: August is when small HVAC problems get expensive.
body_paragraph_1: Your equipment has been running at full load for weeks. Dirt and neglect are the leading causes of heating and cooling system failure, and a clogged filter forces the system to work harder to move the same air — driving up energy use and shortening equipment life.
body_paragraph_2: Filters should be checked monthly through the heavy-use months and changed at least every three months. We handle the inspection, the filters, the coils and the repairs — so nothing gets found the hard way on a 95° afternoon.
tip_headline: A Clean System Is a Cheaper System
tip_body: Replacing a dirty filter with a clean one can cut a unit's energy use by 5 to 15 percent. Pair that with a lighting and energy review and both savings land on the same bill.
note_body: Service cooling equipment in the spring and heating equipment in the fall — contractors book solid the week the weather turns.

headline: Nobody notices clean. Everybody notices the day it slips.
body_paragraph_1: Cleaning is the only service in your building that gets judged every single day and reported only when it fails. By the time a tenant emails you about the restroom, the program has been drifting for weeks.
body_paragraph_2: Drift is a management problem, not a mop problem. Ours is built so that the standard is written down, someone is accountable for it by name, and it gets checked before you have to.
point_1_body: Daily, periodic and deep-clean tasks written by area and frequency — so "clean" means the same thing to your team and ours.
point_2_body: Quality auditors inspect proactively and log what they find. You see the report whether or not anything was wrong.
point_3_body: Our teams work in Corrigo, ServiceChannel, FacilitySource and FEXA, so requests close where you already track them.
aside_body: Cleaning is a people business, and turnover is what breaks it. We hire selectively — only 5% of applicants are brought on — train through master trainers, and give every site a named account executive and client service manager rather than a queue.

hero_alt: Pest technician inspecting a back-of-house corridor
headline: Roaches don't walk in. They arrive on the freight.
body_paragraph_1: German cockroaches don't overwinter outside. They live indoors year-round and arrive the way inventory does — in cardboard, produce crates, pallet wrap and returned equipment. In a warehouse or a retail back room, one contaminated shipment in July is a documented complaint in September.
body_paragraph_2: We treat the harborage, not the surface. Targeted gel and bait placements go into cracks, voids and equipment cavities, with monitors that tell us whether the population is falling between visits — and a written record for your audit file.
note_body: Break down and remove cartons the day they land. Stacked cardboard in a back corridor is harborage, not storage — and it is the first thing an auditor photographs.
points_label: Three entry points we always check
point_1_body: Cardboard and pallets are the most common ride in.
point_2_body: Heat, water and food in one unventilated room.
point_3_body: Vending and appliance motors hold heat overnight.
